v0.1.0-rc.11.title: RelayLink v0.1.0-rc.11
v0.1.0-rc.11.intro: A release candidate after v0.1.0-rc.10 that tightens the management plane, runtime connection limits, and secret-file permissions. The admin endpoint stays plain HTTP and the examples and Docker setup listen on loopback by default. Client connection limits apply immediately, and TCP connections that are silent in both directions close after the server idle timeout.

sections.title: Highlights
items: Example configs and Docker bind dashboard.listenAddress to 127.0.0.1. A non-loopback admin listener writes a SECURITY error to the log and stderr, and the process still starts. The recommended path is still an Agent on the server and an end-to-end encrypted peer channel to the admin UI on 127.0.0.1. This candidate does not add mandatory admin HTTPS.

Passwords longer than 1024 UTF-8 bytes are rejected before PBKDF2. A wrong username still runs PBKDF2. Five failures from the same source lock that source, with backoff from 1 second up to 15 minutes. After a lock expires, one in-flight retry is allowed and failures keep accumulating. The failure cache holds at most 10,000 sources, keeps unexpired history when it prunes, and refuses new sources when it is full of unexpired state.
An existing login session is replaced only after the login-success audit event is stored. If that write fails, login returns 503 and the previous session stays valid.

Before the secret has been checked, ClientNotFound, ClientDisabled, and InvalidSecret are sent to the peer as AuthenticationFailed. The detailed reasons stay in the audit log and server logs. Failures after the secret check stay specific.
Every management response sets Content-Security-Policy (including frame-ancestors 'none'), X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, and X-Frame-Options: DENY. /api stays Cache-Control: no-store.

Client maxConnections and maxPendingConnections take effect immediately. Lowering a limit blocks new slots. Connections that already hold a permit keep it until they finish, and releasing one does not open a slot above the new maximum. Saving a client limit pushes a configuration snapshot to a ready Agent.

Channel and client updates write the JSON first, then switch listeners and the in-memory configuration. If binding fails, the previous file is written back and existing connections stay. A client directory that cannot accept the temp file fails before any listener changes. Deleting a client removes the file first and restores it if the listener update fails.

limits.tcpIdleTimeoutSeconds cancels an established ordinary TCP proxy or authorized peer relay when both directions have been silent for that long, then releases the connection slot. Omitting the field uses 900 seconds; 0 disables idle close. Accepted TCP sockets enable keepalive, and the admin overview shows the active value. Cancellation while waiting for an unauthenticated handshake slot, or a full slot, disposes the accepted socket on the control and data acceptors. RegisterAccepted carries halfCloseDrainTimeoutSeconds and tcpIdleTimeoutSeconds. Current Agents use those values for ordinary TCP relays and for encrypted or plaintext peer copies, including half-close drain. Older peers ignore the new fields. The values follow server.json and are picked up on the next registration.

Client JSON, rewritten server.json, and the SQLite audit and traffic files are readable only by the service account: Unix mode 0600, database directories created for them 0700, and a Windows DACL for the current process identity with inheritance removed. A group- or world-readable secret, private key, client directory, or database is reported as SECURITY in the log and on stderr. Other-writable shared database directories, the process temp directory, /tmp, a filesystem root, and any existing other-writable directory are refused, and the process asks for a RelayLink-only directory. A dedicated database directory is tightened so later WAL and SHM files are not world-readable; a shared parent is not rewritten. The systemd unit sets UMask=0077. Linux deployment docs match the Agent docs: /etc/relaylink and clients are 0700, and secret files are 0600.
Third-party GitHub Actions in CI, release, and Pages are pinned to commit SHAs, with the version tag kept in a comment.

The root README no longer describes the HTTP design as unimplemented. The HTTP design stays Draft and now says the v5 path is on main, while the evaluation and unmeasured capacity sections remain draft. Linux and Windows deployment notes no longer require upgrading Server and Agent together. They follow the v3 TCP / v4 UDP / v5 HTTP matrix and point at the UDP and HTTP operations guides.

sections.title: Upgrade and compatibility
items: NTP1 remains v5, and JSON schemaVersion remains 1. Server continues to accept v3, v4, and v5.
The admin UI remains plain HTTP on loopback by design.

Before upgrading, confirm that secret paths and database directories meet the new permission checks. Windows Docker Desktop bind mounts may need an explicit chmod 0700 or 0600 inside the Linux VM. Omitting tcpIdleTimeoutSeconds now defaults to 900 seconds; set 0 to keep the previous behavior of no application idle timeout.
Otherwise, ordinary TCP/UDP and HTTP proxy behavior is unchanged from v0.1.0-rc.10.

sections.title: Verification and limitations
items: The merged changes #3 (890a282), #4 (d9e03b8), and #2 (e5834f5) passed CI on Ubuntu, Windows, and macOS (Intel and Apple Silicon).

Live Docker smoke on TestClient-01 (Windows, Docker Desktop 29.5.3) at e5834f5: /health/ready and /health/live returned 200; the admin UI returned 200 with CSP, X-Frame-Options, and nosniff; the admin listener inside the container was 127.0.0.1:18080. Docker Desktop network_mode: host is the Linux VM host, not Windows loopback; that was checked with a host-network sidecar.

Known Windows Desktop friction: the admin password is entered interactively on the first compose start, and bind-mount modes need chmod inside the VM. This note does not include multipass or remote test-server verification.
Windows installers are unsigned, and macOS archives are unsigned and not notarized, the same as v0.1.0-rc.10.

v0.1.0-rc.10.title: RelayLink v0.1.0-rc.10
v0.1.0-rc.10.intro: A release candidate that adds HTTP/HTTPS application proxying on the target Agent. Public listeners and encrypted peer access are both checked and forwarded to a fixed web upstream, with tighter WebSocket origin checks, idle timeouts, and client-address header handling.

sections.title: Highlights
items: Adds an HTTP application protocol. The target Agent forwards authorized HTTP/1.1 requests through a Kestrel virtual ingress and YARP, including HTTP/HTTPS, WebSocket, SSE, and streaming bodies. The business ingress does not open an extra operating-system listener, and neither Server nor the caller Agent parses HTTP.

A public channel is accepted by Server and delivered to the target Agent over the data tunnel. Authorized peer access still uses the caller loopback and inner TLS between Agents. Both paths validate and rewrite Host and Origin using the channel policy.
PEM certificates for HTTPS ingress keep their intermediate chain and pass it to Kestrel ServerCertificateChain, without relying on system trust or AIA downloads.

WebSocket Upgrade tokens are recognized individually when separated by commas. Public and peer channels both require a non-empty Origin allowlist. An empty list rejects WebSocket handshakes, including those with a missing Origin or the same origin.

Public WebSocket idle timeout now defaults to 300 seconds and can no longer be set to 0. Peer channels may still set 0 explicitly to disable idle close. A maxWebSocketConnections value of 0 uses the channel connection limit.

Forwarded, X-Forwarded-*, X-Real-IP, True-Client-IP, X-Client-IP, and CF-Connecting-IP are always removed, then forwarding headers are rebuilt from the authenticated ingress. stripRequestHeaders only adds exact header names; an empty list or a null entry cannot re-enable the built-in set. Revoking, disabling, or changing a channel disposes and removes its HTTP host.

sections.title: Upgrade and compatibility
items: NTP1 is now v5. Server accepts v3/v4/v5 and can be upgraded first. Existing v3 Agents keep ordinary and authorized peer TCP, and v4 Agents keep TCP/UDP. HTTP is sent only to v5, and the target Agent must be v5. HTTP peer access also requires a v5 caller with endToEndEncryptionEnabled=true. Versions 1/2, unknown versions, and version changes within a connection are rejected. New Agents do not automatically fall back when connecting to an old Server.

JSON schemaVersion is unchanged. Channels without applicationProtocol stay raw. HTTP channels must use TCP. HTTP policy and certificates take effect after the related Agent restarts; there is no hot reload.

Breaking configuration changes: publicAllowedOrigins and peerAllowedOrigins must both be non-empty Origin allowlists. An empty list can no longer skip origin checks. Public webSocketActivityTimeoutSeconds can no longer be 0; omitting it defaults to 300 seconds. Peer channels may still set 0 explicitly. Before upgrading, fill in the allowlists and check the public idle timeout using the HTTP operations guide.

Back up configuration, identity, Server SQLite data, and certificates before upgrading. Public HTTP has no browser TLS and is only for protected networks or tests that explicitly accept plaintext. Ordinary TCP/UDP behavior remains that of v0.1.0-rc.9.

sections.title: Verification and limitations
items: HTTP proxying and these security fixes passed 137 local unit tests and 81 integration tests with peer TLS enabled. Coverage includes origin rejection, HTTP status lines assembled from partial reads, WebSocket idle and concurrency limits, client-address header stripping, host disposal, and HTTPS intermediate chains. This note does not treat an unreplayed v3/v4 binary matrix or unrun cross-platform CI as completed acceptance.

Real-browser login, cookies, CSRF, and long-running capacity checks remain outstanding. The HTTP requirement stays Accepted and the design stays Draft. HTTP/2, HTTP/3, gRPC, and CONNECT forward proxying are unsupported, and response bodies are not rewritten.
Windows installers are unsigned; macOS packages are unsigned and not notarized. Requirements, design, and ADR review status remain as marked in their respective documents.

v0.1.0-rc.9.title: RelayLink v0.1.0-rc.9
v0.1.0-rc.9.intro: A release candidate adding UDP forwarding and a multipage product website. This rebuilt release includes v3 client compatibility; earlier assets under the same version do not. Download again and verify the latest SHA256SUMS.

sections.title: Highlights
items: Ordinary and authorized peer channels support unicast UDP, isolate sessions by source address and port, and preserve empty datagrams and payloads up to 65507 bytes.
UDP travels through the existing TCP data tunnel with a separate target socket per source. Bounded queues, connection quotas, and idle cleanup retain authentication, security groups, and auditing.

The management UI supports TCP/UDP selection and UDP idle timeout configuration. Configuration snapshots, both dashboards, and read APIs show the protocol; online protocol changes recreate the related listeners.
UDP socket send buffers are at least 128 KiB, fixing large datagram failures caused by macOS defaults.
The product website now has separate home, guide, documentation, and release list/detail pages, with Chinese and English UDP usage, design, and upgrade guidance.

sections.title: Upgrade and compatibility
items: NTP1 is now v4. Server accepts v3/v4, so it can be upgraded first while v3 Agents retain ordinary and authorized peer TCP forwarding. Responses and configuration hashes follow each session version, including mixed old/new peers. Consecutive configuration updates are acknowledged individually, fixing a race that overwrote pending versions and disconnected clients. UDP is sent only to v4 clients and requires all participating Agents to support v4. Versions 1/2, unknown versions, and version changes within a connection are rejected. New Agents do not automatically fall back when connecting to an old Server.
JSON schemaVersion is unchanged. Existing channels without transportProtocol default to TCP. UDP idle timeout defaults to 60 seconds and accepts 1–3600 seconds.

Update installed Windows Agents while preserving configuration and identity. Back up configuration, identity, Server SQLite data, and certificates before upgrading; see the UDP operations guide for details.
Ordinary UDP tunnels retain the plaintext data endpoint; authorized peer traffic uses inner TLS by default. Configure security groups, firewalls, and link protection for your deployment.

sections.title: Verification and limitations
items: CI for UDP and the macOS fix passed website, Linux, Windows, macOS Intel, and Apple Silicon checks. This compatibility fix passed 101 local unit tests and 59 full integration tests, including 9 tests using unmodified rc.8 Agents for ordinary TCP, old-client UDP rejection, mixed old/new peers with TLS or plaintext, and half-close. Peer TLS and the legacy binary matrix were enabled with no skips; the rebuilt tag runs full regular CI again.
UDP tests cover 0/1/32769/65507-byte datagrams, source isolation, idle cleanup, security groups, and online UDP/TCP changes, alongside existing TCP regression tests.

Real UDP applications across public networks, 24-hour capacity checks, and target-environment installation validation remain outstanding. Broadcast, multicast, and IP networking are unsupported. UDP over TCP can cause head-of-line blocking and has no real-time latency guarantee.
Windows installers are unsigned; macOS packages are unsigned and not notarized. Requirements, design, and ADR review status remain as marked in their respective documents.

v0.1.0-rc.8.title: RelayLink v0.1.0-rc.8
v0.1.0-rc.8.intro: A release candidate focused on file logging, connection rejection diagnostics, and Windows Agent configuration saving.

sections.title: Highlights
items: Server and Agent share structured JSONL file logging through Serilog. Agent logging no longer depends on a Windows Event Log source.
Information and Warning logs are retained for 14 days. All files roll daily or at 10 MiB; separate Error and Critical logs are never automatically deleted by age or file count.

Control rejection messages include reasons such as missing or disabled clients, invalid secrets, identity mismatch, and duplicate sessions. Agent logs include the rejection code, reason, and connection stage without secrets, private keys, or application payloads.
Server supports --log-directory. Docker and systemd deployments use /var/lib/relaylink/logs, with Docker logs persisted in the existing data volume.
Windows installation and updates repair LocalService write permissions on agent.json, fixing Unable to save Agent configuration during local JSON imports.
Adds logging requirements, technical design, deployment guidance, and bilingual website explanations.

sections.title: Upgrade and compatibility
items: Use the preserve-state update path for installed Windows Agents. The installer also repairs old configuration permissions. Agent logs are stored in C:\ProgramData\RelayLink\Agent\logs.
The control protocol remains v3 with an optional rejection reason field. Upgrade both Server and Agent for complete reasons; older versions remain compatible but may only show a generic error code.

Connection rejection is a Warning and follows the 14-day retention policy. Permanent retention applies to Error and Critical only. Business diagnostic traces and SQLite audit retain their existing policies.

Read routine runtime events from log files. Container stderr and systemd journal mainly cover startup and logging failures. Operators should monitor capacity and archive permanently retained error files.

sections.title: Verification and limitations
items: The local .NET solution build, 82 unit tests, and 30 integration tests passed. One peer TLS test was skipped by local defaults; the release pipeline enables it.

Coverage includes log rolling and retention, rejection reasons, duplicate sessions, configuration acknowledgement rejection, and sensitive-field checks. Server bootstrap errors and configuration-check mode were also checked locally.

Docker Compose configuration parsing passed. A new container image run and target-environment installation validation remain outstanding. Windows installers are unsigned; macOS packages are unsigned and not notarized.

v0.1.0-rc.7.title: RelayLink v0.1.0-rc.7
v0.1.0-rc.7.intro: A release candidate focused on multi-server Agent connections, local management, and cross-platform delivery.

sections.title: Highlights
items: One Agent can connect to multiple servers with separate client secrets, TLS trust, and runtime state. Channels and access mappings remain managed by their respective servers.

The Agent local dashboard is now a standalone React frontend. Profiles can be added or modified only by importing a single-server JSON file, and can be disabled, re-enabled, or deleted. Disabling disconnects the profile and stops retries while preserving its configuration and identity across restarts.
A standalone pre-start migrator converts legacy single-server configuration and identity state to the servers[] format. Windows, Linux, and macOS startup paths run the migrator before the Agent.
Windows Agent now has both self-contained and framework-dependent program archives and installers. Program files stay in the Agent install root; configuration and state stay in ProgramData.
Fixes the .NET 10 Docker build image selection and UTF-8 BOM handling during Windows configuration migration.
The bilingual product site now explains multi-server Agent connections, JSON import, and profile disabling. The tag triggers both website deployment and software package release.

sections.title: Upgrade and compatibility
items: Use the preserve-state update path for an installed Agent. First install and reconfiguration accept only the new JSON format. Reconfiguration resets managed local state and is unsuitable when retaining the end-to-end identity.
Legacy configuration must be migrated before the new Agent starts. A failed conversion prevents startup while retaining the original configuration and identity state for investigation and retry.
The proxy wire protocol is unchanged. The Agent dashboard binds only to 127.0.0.1; writes require a local session and CSRF token, and read responses do not expose registration secrets.

sections.title: Verification and limitations
items: 63 .NET unit tests and 22 integration tests passed locally. One peer TLS integration test was skipped by the local default; the release pipeline enables it.
The Agent frontend build, formatting check, and isolated local preview passed. Automated coverage checks active-flow disconnection on disable, reconnection on enable, and persistence across restart.
Windows installers are unsigned, and macOS packages are not Developer ID signed or notarized. Installation, connectivity, and capacity still need validation in target environments.

sections.title: Highlights
items: Adds a Linux Docker Engine deployment for the Server with a multi-stage image, initial configuration, start and stop scripts, and host networking for dynamic service ports.

The Windows Agent installer checks operating system architecture, VC++, and the .NET 10 ASP.NET Core Runtime. The Agent is now framework-dependent, and installation scripts support Windows PowerShell 4.0.

sections.title: Security and compatibility

Docker configuration, client secrets, and SQLite data remain in host-mounted directories, outside the image. The stop script preserves them by default.
Windows Agent hosts need the applicable VC++ x64 runtime and .NET 10 ASP.NET Core Runtime x64; installation stops when required dependencies are missing.
The peer protocol is unchanged from rc.5. Upgrades from earlier versions still require coordinated Server and Agent upgrades.

sections.title: Verification and limitations

Docker Compose configuration parsing and a Server Release build passed. Container startup, persistence, and dynamic forwarding still need validation on a Linux Docker host.
The Windows Agent installer compiled, but its dependency screen and full installation and removal still need revalidation on a clean target machine.

v0.1.0-rc.5.title: RelayLink v0.1.0-rc.5
v0.1.0-rc.5.intro: A release candidate focused on client management, local integration, and channel security policy validation.

sections.title: Highlights
items: The admin UI can delete offline clients and blocks deletion while a channel still references the client.
Clients and channels support one or more manually managed tags, with tag filtering in admin lists.
The Agent management endpoint adds a read-only loopback HTTP API for local software to inspect channels and Agent-to-Agent access endpoints.
Agent-to-Agent channels add an end-to-end encryption switch that is enabled by default. When explicitly disabled, traffic is copied directly over the authenticated peer connection.
The peer protocol moves to version 3 and binds the encryption mode into handshake authentication to prevent mismatched configurations.

sections.title: Security and compatibility
items: Agent-to-Server control and raw data links continue to use TLS. The new option affects only peer application traffic on Agent-to-Agent channels.
Unencrypted peer mode retains mutual identity checks, channel authorization, session binding, resource limits, and connection revocation after configuration changes.
Server and all Agents participating in peer access must be upgraded together because older Agents cannot establish version 3 peer sessions.
The local read-only API binds only to `127.0.0.1` and exposes no configuration writes.

sections.title: Verification
items: 40 .NET unit tests and 29 integration tests passed, including peer TLS coverage.
8 admin frontend tests, the production build, and formatting checks passed.
Coverage includes encrypted-default compatibility, plaintext copying, handshake-mode validation, revocation after mode changes, and local API boundaries.

sections.title: Upgrade notes
items: Upgrade the Server and all Agents together to avoid peer protocol version mismatches.
New peer-only channels enable end-to-end encryption by default. Disable it only after explicitly accepting plaintext application traffic on the relay path.
Back up Server configuration, client configuration, Agent identity files, and SQLite databases before upgrading.

sections.title: Highlights

Moves traffic history to minute-level SQLite aggregation with separate standard-proxy and Agent-to-Agent traffic accounting.
Promotes end-to-end identity to client-level certificate fingerprints with first-use registration, pinning, and mismatch rejection.
Suggests an available Server listen port when creating a standard channel.

Stops shipping the unused and potentially incompatible `libe_sqlite3.so` in Linux artifacts.

v0.1.0-rc.2.title: RelayLink v0.1.0-rc.2
v0.1.0-rc.2.intro: This release restructures the tunnel, changes how Agent trust material is delivered, and adds end-to-end acceptance coverage using real database protocols.

sections.title: Highlights
items: Fully separates control and data channels. Application data connections are accepted only after the control channel authenticates.
After binding, standard data channels use simple bidirectional TCP stream copying without parsing or modifying the application protocol.
Completes Agent-to-Agent configuration, Agent identity verification, channel updates, and local endpoint rotation.
Embeds the trusted CA in downloaded Agent configuration instead of requiring a CA file path on the target machine.
Improves management forms and guidance for clients, channels, and Agent-to-Agent access endpoints.
Adds a desktop shortcut for the local read-only status page after Windows Agent installation.
Adds SQL Server and PostgreSQL acceptance scripts covering common queries, joins, and transaction rollback through both standard and encrypted peer paths.

sections.title: Upgrade notes
items: Control and data protocols changed. Upgrade the Server and Agents together and do not mix rc.1 and rc.2 components.
Download a fresh Agent configuration from the admin UI to avoid retaining obsolete trust settings.
Standard proxy data channels do not add encryption. Use application TLS or a protected network path for sensitive traffic.
